text:
Maria: quick heads-up — ran a profile on a 16-shard TP run and saw a surprising memory spike during the forward pass, looks like comm staging + temp allocs are ~28% of per-GPU footprint :eyes:
Ken: can you paste the flamegraph / topo? which model and seq len?
Maria: Llama-13B, seq=2048, batch=4, kernels chosen by runtime default. attached summary: nvprof snapshot ->
```
GPU0 total 40.2 GB
- model weights (quantized) 22.1 GB
- kv cache         6.2 GB
- comm staging     5.6 GB
- temp allocs      3.1 GB
```
Maria: note comm staging was transient but spikes align with kv cache eviction attempts and several async copies.
Sachin: hmm if comm staging is that large it could be per-stream pinned buffers being reserved by our comm layer. Are we allocating a per-shard staging buffer for each NCCL stream?
Ken: I remember we reserved a 512MB workspace per-stream to avoid syncs. If you multiply that across 8 streams and 2 workspaces it's expensive.
Maria: yes I see workspace: 512MB * 8 * 1 = 4GB reserved across some GPUs (we only expected ~1GB). Looks like double-allocation due to fallback path when a kernel didn't accept the fast workspace.
Alexa: idea: make workspace sizing adaptive by kernel acceptance rate. if a kernel refuses fast workspace, reduce reservation for that kernel family and fallback to shared transient pool.
Sachin: also check NCCL envs: are we using NCCL_SHM or enabling P2P? maybe shared memory buffers are duplicating. try NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL or unset to force different path.
Maria: tried toggling NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 earlier — reduced comm staging by ~800MB but latency slightly regressed. tradeoff noted.
Ken: tradeoff is expected. Another lever: reuse a single pinned staging buffer per GPU for all NCCL ops instead of per-stream. We can serialize small chunks or use per-stream offsets into a ring buffer.
Sachin: we should also profile temp allocator fragmentation. the allocator's block size threshold (64MB) causes many small temp allocations to round up into larger granules. If we lower threshold for transient buffers we can reduce internal fragmentation.
Maria: profiler snippet (from runtime trace):
```
[1234.56] kernel_choose -> kernel_xla_fast (accepted)
[1234.60] kv_read -> alloc_temp(48MB)
[1234.61] nccl_send -> stage_pinned(256MB)
[1234.62] kernel_fallback -> alloc_workspace(512MB)
[1234.63] kv_spill -> alloc_temp(120MB)
```
Alexa: small experiment: switch allocator tuning to slab-8 for temps (8MB slab) and have a ring-based comm staging of 1GB per GPU. That should cap worst-case comm staging.
Ken: agree. also consider shrinking TP shard chunking during comm: instead of sending entire shard we stream 128MB windows — lowers peak staging at cost of a bit more NCCL calls. worth benchmarking.
Sachin: can we avoid double-copy for KV cache read? I think we copy from device->staging pinned->nccl, maybe we can do device->device on some topologies. Need to query P2P availability per pair.
Maria: good call — topology map shows many pairs are NVLINK-connected. we should prefer peer-to-peer when available and only fallback to host staging otherwise.
Alexa: I'll sketch a patch: 1) add per-GPU ring staging allocator (configurable cap) 2) allocator: lower rounding for temp allocs, add slab buckets for <16MB 3) comm: stream-windowed shard sends + prefer P2P where possible 4) kernel selection: annotate kernels with workspace-acceptance so runtime can avoid reserving duplicate workspaces
Maria: that would address the double reservation and the fragmentation. can you also add a perf-counter for "staging_peak" and "temp_frag_pct" so we can track regressions over time?
Alexa: yep will add counters and a small grafana dashboard.
Ken: quick micro-bench plan: run 3 configs on the same model/seq/batch — baseline, ring-staging+slab allocator, ring+slab+windowed streaming. measure peak mem, 99p latency, and tail OOM counts.
Sachin: also include a run with NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=1 to surface the latency/mem tradeoff.
Maria: I'll run the baseline and the NCCL_SHM_DISABLE run now on the infra node pool. tagging @infra-bot to spin up an extra 4xA100 node for the bigger run.
infra-bot: requested nodes allocated: 4xA100 pool-rapid-2. ETA 3m. :white_check_mark:
Maria: baseline done: peak staging 5.6GB, temp frag 18%, no OOMs. NCCL_SHM_DISABLE run: staging 4.8GB, temp frag 17%, 2x 2s latency regressions, no OOMs.
AlexA: (reaction) :+1: interesting.
Ken: next steps: Alexa to implement allocator + ring staging prototype; Maria to run the micro-bench harness; Sachin to instrument P2P paths and measure savings; I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to review numbers.
Maria: thanks everyone. I'll paste logs and flamegraphs into the thread when the micro-bench finishes. :coffee:
